metaDescription: 2026 Maiden's Tower guide: Karaköy and Salacak boat piers, €35 ticket fees, sunset views from Salacak, and walking routes to Üsküdar's mosques.
quickAnswer: Reopened as a restored monument-museum on its Bosphorus islet, Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) charges foreign visitors €35 (€27 + €8 audio guide/museum ticket) in 2026, plus a separate 110 TL boat fare. Official shuttles depart from Karaköy (Ziraat Bank pier) and Salacak, though watching the tower at sunset from the Salacak promenade is free and iconic.

body.text: How do boats depart from Karaköy and Üsküdar to Maiden's Tower?

Official museum shuttle boats serve Maiden's Tower from Karaköy (the pier in front of Ziraat Bank) and Salacak on the Üsküdar–Harem coast, with the boat crossing priced separately at 110 TL ([Müze Kart Kız Kulesi](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?sectionId=KZK02&distId=MRK)). During active Salacak coastal works, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism routes primary departures through the Karaköy Ziraat Bank pier, so confirm active pier status on [kizkulesi.gov.tr/en/visit](https://kizkulesi.gov.tr/en/visit) on the day you go.

From Karaköy, the crossing takes roughly 15 minutes and return boats generally depart the islet on a fixed hourly cycle, giving you around 45 to 60 minutes to explore the tower exhibitions and balcony ([MerrySails Maiden's Tower Guide](https://merrysails.com/guides/maidens-tower)). From Salacak (when operating), the hop across the 200-meter channel takes just a few minutes. Avoid high-wind winter afternoons when Bosphorus chop can briefly suspend shuttle sailings.
What are the 2026 ticket prices and visiting hours after restoration?

According to the official [Maiden's Tower Visit Page](https://kizkulesi.gov.tr/en/visit), foreign visitors without a Museum Pass Türkiye pay 27 + 8 Euro (€35 total) for the museum entrance ticket and audio guide, excluding the 110 TL boat transport fee. Museum Pass Türkiye holders enter the tower free of charge and pay only the 110 TL boat fare.

Following its extensive multi-year structural restoration—which stripped away late 20th-century concrete additions and restored the historic wooden cupola and stone masonry—the tower operates daily as a museum rather than a sit-down restaurant. Opening hours run daily (typically 09:00 onward, with last boat departures shifting seasonally in late afternoon), so always verify the day's final boat time on [kizkulesi.gov.tr/en/visit](https://kizkulesi.gov.tr/en/visit) before heading to the pier.

body.text: Is visiting inside better or watching it at sunset from Salacak?

For most travelers on a single-visit budget, watching Maiden's Tower at sunset from the Salacak promenade in Üsküdar beats paying €35 to go inside—because from inside the tower, you cannot see the tower itself. Going inside makes the most sense if you already hold a Museum Pass Türkiye or specifically want the 360-degree balcony view facing both continents.

Along the Salacak waterfront, locals gather an hour before sundown on stone steps and terraced tea spots facing west. As the sun drops behind the domes of Topkapı Palace, Hagia Sophia, and the Blue Mosque across the strait, the white tower lights up against deep violet water. Arrive 45 minutes before sunset to claim a front-row seat with a glass of hot Turkish tea and a fresh simit.
How do you pair it with Üsküdar's historic mosques?

Üsküdar's ferry square sits just a 15-minute level walk north of Salacak, placing three remarkable Ottoman mosques within a compact waterfront triangle. Start in Üsküdar Square around 14:30, visit the mosques between afternoon prayers, and stroll south along the shore toward Salacak in time for golden hour.
Use this afternoon walking checklist on the Asian shore:

items: 14:30 Mihrimah Sultan (İskele) Mosque: Step straight off the Üsküdar ferry or Marmaray train into Mimar Sinan's 1548 waterfront mosque, commissioned by Sultan Suleiman's daughter ([Üsküdar Municipality – Mihrimah Sultan Mosque](https://www.uskudar.bel.tr/en/main/pages/mihrimah-sultan-mosque/315)).
15:15 Yeni Valide Mosque: Walk two minutes inland across the square to admire its ornate 18th-century Ottoman stonework, arched courtyard, and open-air birdhouses.

16:00 Şemsi Paşa Mosque: Head five minutes southwest to the shoreline for Mimar Sinan's smallest imperial-style waterside mosque, famously designed where intersecting Bosphorus breezes keep birds off the courtyard ([Üsküdar Municipality – Şemsi Paşa Mosque](https://www.uskudar.bel.tr/en/main/pages/semsi-pasha-mosque/311)).
16:30 Salacak sunset walk: Continue 10 minutes south along the coastal walkway until Maiden's Tower aligns directly with the Sultanahmet skyline across the water.

faq.q: Does Maiden's Tower still have a restaurant inside after the restoration?
faq.a: No. After its structural restoration, Maiden's Tower reopened as a monument-museum focused on its history and 360-degree viewing balcony rather than a formal dining restaurant.

faq.q: Is the boat ride included in the Museum Pass Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Museum Pass Türkiye covers the tower entrance fee, but pass holders still pay the separate 110 TL boat transportation fee at the pier.

faq.q: How long is the walk from Üsküdar ferry pier to Salacak?
faq.a: The flat coastal promenade from Üsküdar Pier past Şemsi Paşa Mosque to the Maiden's Tower viewpoint at Salacak takes roughly 15 minutes on foot.

faq.q: How do I reach Üsküdar from Sultanahmet or Karaköy?
faq.a: Ride the Marmaray commuter rail one stop under the Bosphorus from Sirkeci to Üsküdar in four minutes, or take a scenic 15-minute Şehir Hatları ferry from Eminönü, Karaköy, or Beşiktaş.

faq.q: Can I enter Maiden's Tower without booking weeks in advance?
faq.a: Tickets and boat slots are sold at the departure pier and online; in peak summer and weekends, arriving earlier in the day avoids long queues for the timed shuttle boats.

faq.q: What is the best season for sunset photos at Salacak?
faq.a: Clear spring (April–May) and autumn (September–October) evenings offer crisp visibility across the Historic Peninsula without the summer haze or winter Bosphorus fog.
